study_type_evidence.quote: The plasma pharmacokinetic (PK) profile and biodistribution of peptide-loaded nanoparticles (1 mg/kg equivalent dose of free peptide) vs. free peptide were assessed in mice after intravenous (IV; via tail vein) dosing.
Each dialysis tube was sealed, placed into a capped container containing 5 mL PBS, and then placed into an incubator maintained at 37 °C

in_vivo_species.quote: Wild-type C57BL/6J mice (male, 10–12 weeks old) were purchased from the Animal Resources Centre (Perth, WA, Australia).

in_vitro_detail: Cell-free in vitro release study: peptide-loaded nanoparticle suspension in dialysis tubing (MWCO 10 kDa) against 5 mL PBS at 37 °C with horizontal shaking, sampled at 1, 3, 6, 24, 30, 48, 54 and 72 h and quantified by LC-MS/MS. Particle characterisation by DLS, zeta potential and TEM. No cell-culture work reported.

notes: The first sentence of Section 3.3 reads 'significantly reduced elimination half-life in mice compared to the peptide itself', which contradicts every other statement in the same paragraph and the Conclusions ('a significant increase in the terminal half-life'); treated as a typographical error in the paper. The values 0.17 h (plasma) and 0.33 h (spinal cord) are cited in this paper as previously reported literature values, not as data generated here - the value generated in this study for the free peptide is 0.84 h. Other PK parameters reported in the body: AUC0-t 3825.7 ng.h/mL (free peptide) vs 18,665.6 (nanoparticle, units printed as 'g.h/mL', evidently a typo); MRT 0.76 h vs 32.61 h. Cmax and Tmax are not reported anywhere in the body. Plasma sampling times listed as 0.04, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 1, 4, 6, 24 h (the repeated '1' appears in the source) plus 48, 72, 96, 120 h for the nanoparticle group. Zolazepam and xylazine are listed in Materials but no anaesthesia procedure is described in the body.
